E1.evidence: The issue gives a complete parameter file and reproduction steps ("Launch Nav2 on both Ubuntu 22.04 and Ubuntu 24.04 with ROS 2 Jazzy using this parameter file ... Observe `/cmd_vel` and compare the `linear.x` output") and the observed effect "On Ubuntu 24.04, maximum speed is limited to \~0.25 m/s." -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/5386. The reporter later identified the cause and the maintainer closed it: "Great! I'm glad you found your issue :-)" -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/5386#issuecomment-3128273470. The linked backport PR 6336 was merged to jazzy on 2025-08-11.

units_identified: odometry provider publishing /odometry/filtered (not identified by package in the source)
E2.evidence: The reported composition is one unit (nav2_mppi_controller) run at two distro revisions with the same user parameter file; the parameter file is that node's own configuration, not a separate unit. The reporter's diagnosis is a behaviour change inside the controller: "I think the following parameters are not effective in the HUMBLE version. ax_max: 3.0 ax_min: -3.0 ay_min: -3.0 ay_max: 3.0 az_max: 3.5 and it is effective in JAZZY. It seems that the small acceleration value causes the vehicle to slow down." -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/5386#issuecomment-3125122390. The humble optimizer.cpp has no ax_max/az_max parameters, while jazzy reads them (`getParam(s.base_constraints.ax_max, "ax_max", 3.0f);`) and clamps the control sequence with `float max_delta_vx = s.model_dt * s.constraints.ax_max;`; both branches seed the first rollout state from the measured speed (humble: `xt::noalias(xt::view(state.vx, xt::all(), 0)) = state.speed.linear.x;`). The merged fix only adds an opt-in seeding mode inside the controller: "Fixes a Humble to Jazzy regression: MPPI seeds rollouts from lagging odometry instead of its own last command" and "Defaulting to false so no behavior change unless opted in" -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/pull/6336. The only candidate peer (the odometry source) sends a correct measured velocity; no value, frame, unit, name or timing crossing the boundary is wrong, and the slowdown follows from the controller's own acceleration clamp applied from the measured speed with any truthful odometry of a base that lags its setpoint (PR 5617: "MPPI will get the current odometry and add small velocity step for next setpoint every control iteration" -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/pull/5617).

E3.evidence: If treated as a composition, the reporter's comparison is an UPGRADE of nav2_mppi_controller (humble -> jazzy 1.3.7) under an unchanged parameter file; the PR 5617 mechanism is a PAIR (odometry feeds the controller). Not evaluated further because E2 fails.

E4.evidence: Observed effect: "On Ubuntu 24.04, maximum speed is limited to \~0.25 m/s." -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/5386

notes: The issue was closed by the reporter as a parameter/tuning finding (acceleration limits that exist and are enforced on jazzy but not on humble; the migration guide was pointed to by the maintainer). The packet's fix ref PR 6336 is a jazzy backport (merge commit 3f71f94b105b6731953a137561e8c27acc3e3acf, merged 2026-08-11) of main PR 5617 (merge commit 8dbc92910b020b19b9891849b3ee7cb92e1b3b03) that adds an `open_loop` parameter (default false) so the optimizer seeds `state_.speed` from `last_command_vel_` instead of `robot_speed`; it cross-references 5386 but was not opened in response to it and does not show the reporter's composition working. An alternative reading would treat the robot base / odometry source and the controller as two units with a dynamics assumption (maintainer in issue 5214: "all controllers in Nav2 assume that your robot has properly setup robot controllers to be able to execute commands given" -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/5214#issuecomment-2927731729); I did not adopt it because the source never identifies the odometry-providing unit, the odometry values are correct, and the fix changes only the controller's own seeding logic. A second reporter (issue 5694, diff_drive_controller odometry) saw the same symptom and was likewise pointed to the migration guides.
